content: Triamterene and hydrochlorothiazide are prescribed to treat high blood pressure and edema, which is the retention of excess fluid in body tissues. This medication is particularly useful for patients with low potassium levels or for those in whom low potassium levels could pose a health risk. The combination of triamterene and hydrochlorothiazide belongs to a class of drugs known as diuretics, or water pills. It works by prompting the kidneys to eliminate excess water and sodium through urine while minimizing the loss of potassium. This medication is available in capsule and tablet forms and is taken orally, usually once a day. It is important to take it at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. While this medication helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure it. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Triamterene and hydrochlorothiazide may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about this, ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to triamterene, hydrochlorothiazide, sulfonamide-derived medications (sulfa drugs), or any other drugs. Do not take this medication if you are already taking amiloride, spironolactone, or other medications containing triamterene. Provide your doctor and pharmacist with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention specific drugs such as amphotericin B, ACE inhibitors, anticoagulants, barbiturates, digoxin, laxatives, lithium, diabetes medications, gout medications, NSAIDs, oral steroids, potassium supplements, and others. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney stones, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), diabetes, gout, or thyroid, heart, kidney, or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, let your doctor know. Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. If you become pregnant while on this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as this medication may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Be aware that this medication may cause dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting, especially when you get up too quickly from a lying position. This is more common when you first start taking the medication and may be worsened by alcohol consumption. To minimize this effect, rise slowly from bed, allowing your feet to rest on the floor for a few minutes before standing. Follow your doctor’s dietary instructions, which may include a reduced-sodium diet. Avoid potassium-containing salt substitutes and foods high in potassium, such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice, while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. This medication may cause side effects. Minor side effects include gas, frequent urination, dizziness, and headache. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention and include rash or hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, upper stomach pain, swelling or tenderness in the stomach area, upset stomach, vomiting, fever, rapid pulse, extreme tiredness, unusual bruising or bleeding, loss of appetite, yellowing of the skin or eyes, flu-like symptoms, muscle weakness or cramps, numbness or tingling sensations, inability to move arms or legs, slow or irregular heartbeat, severe dry mouth, severe thirst, muscle pain or fatigue, and decreased urination. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the person has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include increased urination, upset stomach, vomiting, weakness or tiredness, and fever. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order lab tests to monitor your body’s response to this medication. Inform your doctor and lab personnel that you are taking this medication before undergoing any tests. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
